_comment: MY per-part understanding, in plain language, for the user to check and correct.
The bench SYNTHESISES a baseline for every part from its role, title and dimensions
(see ROLE_DEF / ROLE_MODEL in part.js). This file is the hand-written layer on top:
where I have looked hard at a part, I write what it is, how I model it, how it fits,
and -- kept honest and separate -- what is DERIVED (read off a manual/photo/dimension),
what is ASSUMED (my inference, could be wrong), and what is UNKNOWN.
Only parts I have actually studied need an entry. A missing entry is not an error;
it means the bench is showing the role-based baseline and I have not reviewed it yet.
Give feedback against any line and I will move it between derived/assumed/unknown or fix it.
Fields: what, model, fits, confidence(high|medium|low), derived[], assumed[], unknown[].

ST-050.what: The Jikaro Fire Ring Table: an octagonal table (1120mm across, 400mm tall) with an open centre for a fire pit or ring, standing on eight wire legs. A standalone table, not part of the IGT rail system.
ST-050.model: jikaroGroup -- one octagon ring (outer 1120, central opening 600, extruded flat) on eight U-hairpin legs, one at each octagon vertex, each hairpin spread TANGENTIALLY along the edge with a notched foot bar.
ST-050.fits: Standalone. No hooks or brackets; it does not join the frame rail. Snow Peak groups it with the layout tables by height (400mm datum), not by connection.
derived: octagon outline and the central opening are traced off the top-view photograph
overall 1120mm and height 400mm are from the catalogue

eight U-hairpin legs at the eight vertices (two per trapezoid segment, near its corners), spread tangentially -- from the disassembled photo a009 AND the pair marks D,E, which each land a wire on the +x corner pair (vertices near 18° and 72°)
assumed: opening 600mm and slant-edge 365mm (ring proportions eyeballed from the photo)
hairpin half-width ~66mm and foot notch ~32mm (leg WIRE detail eyeballed; D,E fix position, not the hairpin's own width)
unknown: whether the feet sit exactly on the vertex radius or a little inboard -- two noisy marks can't tell ±20mm

CK-153TR.what: Renewed Bamboo IGT Sliding Extension (short): a small bamboo board (423x220) that grips the frame's long rail and cantilevers outward, adding a shelf beside the table.
CK-153TR.model: slideExtGroup -- a bamboo slab with two under-brackets that clip over the rail; the board top carries the real grain/logo texture (from the alt_02 top-view photo).
CK-153TR.fits: Clips onto the frame's LONG side (the rail), not the short end. Slides freely along the rail (the planner snaps it in 25mm steps). Two CK-153TR end to end span the same length as a Three Unit Frame (846mm).
derived: dimensions 423x220x33 from the catalogue
top texture is the real alt_02 orthographic top view
mounts on the long rail (manual/photo)
assumed: bracket shape and the 220mm cantilever reach
25mm slide snap is a planner convenience, not a real detent
unknown: how far two of them must overlap/space to avoid fouling each other on the same rail

CK-154TR.what: Renewed Bamboo IGT Sliding Extension Long: the longer sibling of CK-153TR (548x220), same idea -- a bamboo board that grips the rail and reaches out.
CK-154TR.model: slideExtGroup, same builder as CK-153TR, longer board.
CK-154TR.fits: Clips onto the frame's LONG rail and slides. Two CK-154TR end to end span the same length as a Four Unit Frame (1096mm).
derived: dimensions 548x220x33 from the catalogue
two of them = Four Unit Frame length (1096mm)
assumed: bracket shape and cantilever reach, shared with CK-153TR
unknown: overlap/spacing rule when several share one rail

CK-117TR.what: Renewed Bamboo IGT Table Long: a full-length (1096mm) bamboo tabletop that hooks onto a frame end and runs the length out -- the four-unit extension surface.
CK-117TR.model: tableGroup -- a flat bamboo slab, with the plan-view photo laid under it in the same frame so the hook and bracket positions can be checked against the board.
CK-117TR.fits: Hooks onto the frame's SHORT end (its hooks drop into the black end pieces) and carries straight on for four units. Takes its host frame's leg SKU.
derived: 1096mm = four units (250*4+96) from the dimension
hooks on the short end, from the frame-fittings plan view
assumed: exact hook mm positions where not yet measured off a photo

CK-116TR.what: Renewed Bamboo IGT Table Regular: the 846mm (three-unit) bamboo tabletop; same as CK-117TR one size down.
CK-116TR.model: tableGroup -- flat bamboo slab with the plan view underlaid.
CK-116TR.fits: Hooks onto the frame's short end and carries on for three units.
derived: 846mm = three units (250*3+96)

CK-119TR.what: Bamboo Right Corner Extension: a 496mm square bamboo board that turns the run 90 degrees at a corner (the LEFT-hand version is CK-118TR).
CK-119TR.model: tableGroup -- a square flat slab. The corner turn is what makes it special: its hook edge and bracket edge are PERPENDICULAR, so the layout changes direction through it.
CK-119TR.fits: Hooks on one edge, offers brackets on an adjacent (not opposite) edge, so the run leaves at 90 degrees. Left/right decides which way it turns.
derived: 496mm square from the catalogue
corner (perpendicular hook vs bracket edge) from the role and the plan view
assumed: which physical edge is hook vs bracket for R vs L, where not yet measured

CK-150.what: IGT Four Unit Frame: the rigid four-unit (1096mm) leg frame -- the backbone a run is built on. Silver corner plates carry the leg sockets; black end pieces carry the holes an extension's hooks drop into.
CK-150.model: frameGroup -- the frame cross-section swept to length, with the hook-holes along the ends and sockets at the corners.
CK-150.fits: The central node: takes legs at the corners, extensions hook onto its short ends, sliding boards clip on its long rails, and frames join frame-to-frame via the rail joint (XCK-128).
derived: 1096mm = four units
hook-holes on the ends and leg sockets at corners, from the underside plan view
assumed: exact cross-section profile where read off a single photo

CK-149.what: IGT Three Unit Frame: the 846mm rigid frame; CK-150 one size down.
CK-149.fits: Same as CK-150: legs at corners, extensions on the ends, boards on the rails, joins to other frames.
derived: 846mm = three units

CK-904.what: Collapsible IGT 4 Unit Frame: the folding version of the four-unit frame -- rails that collapse for packing rather than a rigid weld.
CK-904.fits: Same role as CK-150 (legs, extensions, rails, frame joints) but folds flat; pairs with the collapsible rails (CK-904-1).
derived: 1096mm = four units
collapsible, from the title and the separate rails part
assumed: how the fold changes the rail cross-section vs the rigid frame

GS-450R-US.what: Flat Burner: a low, flat single-burner stove sized to drop into two IGT units (270x410), sitting flush in the frame like a tabletop.
GS-450R-US.model: moduleGroup (a slot module) with a real top texture cropped from the burner's own top-view photo.
GS-450R-US.fits: Drops into the frame as a 2-unit slot module -- its rim rests on the rails, the body hangs below.
derived: 270x410 = 2 units wide
top texture from the a016 top-view photo
assumed: how deep the body hangs below the rail line

XCK-128-01.what: Multi Function Table Rail Joint (2-piece set): the little joint that ties one frame's long rail to the next, so two frames read as one continuous run.
XCK-128-01.model: plateGroup -- a small connecting plate; it is hardware, not a surface.
XCK-128-01.fits: Joins frame long-rail to frame long-rail. It is why frames line up side by side; without it they are just two tables near each other.
derived: joins the long rails, from the manual
assumed: exact plate geometry (modelled as a generic plate)

GF-010.what: Garden Unit Table Wood Insert: a wood insert for the Garden Unit Table. Currently EXCLUDED from the planner.
GF-010.fits: Excluded -- it belongs to the Garden Unit Table ecosystem, which the planner does not cover yet.
derived: excluded, by decision
